messages: Erin: Quick PRD intake — customer (FinCo) reported repeated tail latency spikes for Dedicated during morning bursts. Problem: some tenants see 2-3x p95 on cold-capacity growth which breaks their SLAs.

Erin: Proposed deliverable = a lightweight launch checklist + acceptance criteria + rollback/playbook for tenant-level SLA fallback. Not asking for multi-region or full private deployment changes — keep scope narrow.

Erin: Goals: 1) automatic per-tenant fallback to lower-cost model-variant when p95 > target for 3 consecutive minutes; 2) clear runbook and metrics; 3) canary on 2 pilot tenants. Non-goals: rewriting serving runtime or full autoscale redesign.
Alice: can you put numbers on the target p95 and the allowed degradation? we need concrete thresholds to write alerts.
Erin: Target: p95 < 350ms for tenant API calls (for this customer's workload). Acceptable fallback: up to +30% p95 compared to baseline but must keep tail bounded and failure rates <= 0.1%.

Ben: acceptance criteria sketch:
```
- Metric: tenant.p95_over_time <= 350ms for 95% of 1h windows post-rollout
- If p95 > 350ms for 3m, route traffic to compatible quantized model variant with preserved API semantics
- No more than 0.1% 5xx spike attributable to the fallback path
- Automated rollback if regression detected by eval harness within 24h
```

Carla: edge cases to call out: cold-start + batching interactions, model-variant semantic drift (we need eval prompts), tenant with custom routing rules, and quota enforcement when fallback increases token cost.
Gabe: dependency list: routing policy config UI changes, per-tenant metric groups, eval harness that can run pre/post checks, and a canary toggle in console. Owner?
Erin: owner = @carla for spec + runbook. @ben to own rollout automation (routing + canary). @alice to own metrics + alerts. Timeline: EOW agree on scope, 2-week spike to prototype, pilot in 4 weeks.
Alice: for metrics we need a new tenant-level histogram and a synthetic prompt set. I can reuse the eval suite but need model-variant artifact tags from model onboarding.

Ben: implementation note — routing fallback should be a policy that can be expressed as JSON. Example policy snippet: 
```
{"trigger": {"metric": "tenant.p95", "window": "3m", "threshold_ms": 350},
 "action": {"route_to": "model-v1-quantized", "reason": "sla-fallback"}}
```
Carla: we should add an acceptance test: run the workload against baseline and fallback variant and measure semantic similarity > 0.95 (embedding cosine) on the eval prompt set.

Erin: success metrics to report in PRD: mean p95 improvement, number of fallbacks triggered in pilot, semantic similarity delta, and cost delta per tenant. Also: documented rollback time and incidents avoided.
Gabe: risk: fallback could increase token spend. Mitigation: limit fallback duration per tenant per hour, and add budget guardrails. Add to non-goals if we can't instrument cost quickly.
Alice: question on rollout: do we want a gradual % ramp or immediate switch for affected requests? i vote gradual ramp with immediate safety cut.
Ben: agreed on ramp. Canary plan: 0.1% -> 1% -> 10% over 6 hours, monitor p95/5xx/semantic drift. Auto-stop if any metric breaches alert thresholds.

Erin: next steps: Carla to draft the short PRD (problem, goals, acceptance criteria, non-goals, risks, owners, timeline). Ben + Alice to validate policies and metrics. Review on Thurs 11am. Anyone object?
Carla: ok, I'll draft and link in this thread. Expect first pass by Wed afternoon.
Alice: I'll provision the tenant metrics and a synthetic eval set by Wed EOD.
Ben: I'll prototype the policy engine mapping and a test harness this week.
